items.prompt: Find the first index where a pattern occurs in a text, with a worst-case guarantee of O(n + m).
items.why: Pattern matching with a worst-case bound → KMP (prefix function). A naive window re-compare is O(n · m) in the worst case.

items.prompt: Decide whether string b can be obtained by rotating string a (moving a prefix to the end).
items.why: A string-specific trick: b is a rotation of a iff they have the same length and b occurs in a + a.

items.prompt: Return the length of the longest substring that contains at most two distinct characters.
items.why: Longest contiguous substring under a maintainable condition → dynamic sliding window with a count map.

items.prompt: Produce the n-th term of the sequence 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221, … where each term describes the runs of digits in the previous one.
items.why: Pure simulation: scan runs with an index and build the next term with a list + join. Nothing is reused between terms.

items.prompt: Find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of a string.
items.why: A palindrome built from a subsequence (gaps allowed) → interval DP over (i, j).

items.prompt: Check whether a string of brackets ()[]{} is properly nested.
items.why: Nesting → push openers, pop and match on closers.

items.prompt: Parse a string into a 32-bit integer: skip leading spaces, read an optional sign and digits, stop at the first non-digit, clamp on overflow.
items.why: Rule-by-rule parsing with an index (atoi). The difficulty is in the edge cases, not the algorithm.

items.prompt: Decide whether two strings are anagrams of each other.
items.why: Just compare letter counts: a count map or a 26-array in O(n). Sorting both is O(n log n).

items.prompt: Return the words of a sentence in reverse order, with single spaces, even if the input has extra spaces.
items.why: Split on whitespace, reverse, join once. Or, in place: reverse the whole buffer, then each word. It's a build-don't-concatenate exercise.
